"ROADBOUND — 3D Mobile Driving Game

Create a complete, polished, playable 3D mobile driving game called ROADBOUND.

Roadbound is an endless arcade driving game inspired by the accessible, cartoonish style of Crash of Cars, featuring traffic dodging, vehicle customization, satisfying collisions, and a beautiful world that reacts dynamically to music.

The game should feel smooth, colorful, responsive, and visually polished.

1. VISUAL STYLE

Create a vibrant, stylized 3D world featuring:

- Smooth, detailed low-poly cartoon graphics.
- Rich, saturated colors with deep contrast.
- Beautiful golden-hour sunset lighting.
- Orange, pink, and purple skies.
- Soft shadows and atmospheric distance.
- Smooth reflective asphalt roads.
- Rolling hills, forests, farms, fences, and fields.
- Colorful trees, grass, bushes, and roadside details.
- Occasional barns, houses, and other countryside structures.
- Dynamic lighting and subtle bloom.
- Attractive, consistent materials and smooth vehicle surfaces.

The graphics should resemble a polished commercial mobile game.

Avoid excessively blocky environments, primitive-looking graphics, transparent vehicle bodies, and mismatched materials.

Use a third-person chase camera positioned behind and slightly above the player's vehicle.

The camera should follow smoothly, including gentle movement when turning or colliding.

2. CORE GAMEPLAY

Roadbound is an endless driving game where the player travels forward along a road filled with moving traffic.

The player's objective is to survive as long as possible, weave through traffic, and earn the highest score.

Implement:

- Automatically accelerating player vehicles.
- Smooth manual left/right steering.
- Responsive traffic avoidance.
- Procedurally extending roads.
- Increasing traffic difficulty over time.
- Different AI traffic vehicles.
- Cars that change lanes and move at different speeds.
- Natural traffic movement.
- Satisfying vehicle-to-vehicle collisions.
- Arcade-style bumping and pushing physics.
- Smooth handling without excessive sliding.

Collision system

Collisions should not instantly end the game.

Instead:

- Colliding with traffic causes a satisfying physical bump.
- Vehicles can push and knock each other sideways.
- Player vehicles remain controllable after collisions.
- Three collisions within 4.5 seconds trigger a game over.
- If enough time passes, the collision counter resets.

Display a game-over screen showing the player's final score, distance traveled, and a restart button.

3. MOBILE CONTROLS

Design specifically for Android smartphones in portrait orientation.

Controls:

- Hold the left half of the screen to steer left.
- Hold the right half to steer right.
- Steering must be smooth and proportional to holding duration.
- Double-tap either side to perform a quick lane change.
- Vehicle automatically accelerates.
- No separate accelerator or brake buttons.

Keep gameplay controls nearly invisible.

The driving screen should feel cinematic and uncluttered.

Include a pause button in the upper corner.

4. VEHICLES

Start with two completely playable vehicles:

Vehicle 1: Pickup Truck

- Compact, cartoonish pickup.
- Simple but recognizable proportions.
- Defined hood, cab, and truck bed.
- Properly aligned body panels.
- Smooth, opaque body surfaces.
- Black window borders.
- Dark tinted windows.
- Chrome front and rear bumpers.
- Detailed headlights and taillights.
- Functional-looking wheels.
- Shiny metallic paint.

Vehicle 2: Car

- Small, sporty cartoon-style car.
- Smooth rounded body.
- Low, attractive proportions.
- Clearly defined windshield and windows.
- Detailed headlights and taillights.
- Reflective paint.
- Matching visual quality to the pickup.

Both vehicles must have:

- Rotating wheels.
- Smooth steering animations.
- Working headlights.
- Brake lights.
- Turn signals.
- Distinct handling characteristics.
- Properly aligned body parts.
- Consistent paint colors across all panels.

Avoid overly realistic or excessively blocky vehicle models.

5. GARAGE AND CUSTOMIZATION

The main menu should be a beautiful interactive garage.

Display the selected vehicle on a rotating presentation platform.

Include:

- Play button.
- Switch Vehicle button.
- Customize button.
- Settings button.

Players can customize:

- Vehicle paint colors.
- Standard and metallic paint finishes.
- Wheel appearance.
- Animated full-body vehicle skins.

Metallic paint should be especially reflective, glossy, and shiny, with believable environmental reflections.

Full-body skins should cover the vehicle and feature smooth animations.

Do not include vehicle attachments, external accessories, trails, or additional cosmetic effects.

The customization system must work on both available vehicles.

6. MUSIC AND RADIO

Music is one of Roadbound's most important features.

Create a functioning in-game radio with:

- Built-in music playlist.
- Song selection.
- Play and pause.
- Next and previous song.
- Playlist management.
- Ability to import audio files from the player's device.

Imported music should play during driving.

Music must continue smoothly without restarting between gameplay transitions unless the player chooses otherwise.

7. MUSIC-REACTIVE WORLD

Make the environment react visibly to whatever music is playing.

Use real-time audio analysis to detect bass, beats, and overall music intensity.

Examples:

- Trees subtly bounce with the beat.
- Grass and bushes pulse.
- Streetlights and environmental lights change brightness.
- The sunset glows more intensely during strong beats.
- Roadside colors shift rhythmically.
- The sky subtly changes saturation.
- A circular visualizer surrounding the distant sun pulses with the music.
- Reflections and environmental lighting react to musical intensity.

Bass should produce stronger reactions than quiet sounds.

Animations should feel smooth, synchronized, and visually pleasing.

The world must react to both built-in songs and imported audio.

Avoid excessive flashing or uncomfortable camera shaking.

8. SCORING

Implement a scoring system that rewards:

- Distance traveled.
- Time survived.
- Successfully avoiding traffic.
- Close calls.
- Consecutive near misses.
- Skillful driving.

Include a combo multiplier that increases through successful driving.

Display:

- Current score.
- Distance.
- Combo multiplier.
- Current song information.

Keep the interface small and unobtrusive.

9. WORLD GENERATION

Create an endless, continuously streaming countryside environment.

Include:

- Curved and straight roads.
- Multiple traffic lanes.
- Painted road markings.
- Smooth terrain.
- Trees and forests.
- Farmland.
- Open grassy fields.
- Fences and roadside barriers.
- Small rural buildings.
- Distant hills.
- Beautiful sunset scenery.

Terrain and scenery should extend naturally into the distance without noticeable gaps.

Objects should transition smoothly as the player travels.

Avoid obvious repetition whenever possible.

10. PERFORMANCE

Optimize the game specifically for Android.

Requirements:

- Target stable 30+ FPS on midrange devices.
- Efficient low-poly models.
- Optimized lighting and shadows.
- Object pooling for traffic.
- Efficient procedural world generation.
- Level-of-detail optimization.
- Responsive touchscreen controls.
- Smooth vehicle physics.
- Fast loading times.
- Proper portrait-screen scaling.

11. GAME FEEL

Roadbound should feel like a polished arcade driving game.

Prioritize:

1. Extremely smooth driving.
2. Satisfying traffic collisions.
3. Beautiful, vibrant graphics.
4. Responsive touch controls.
5. Enjoyable vehicle customization.
6. A music-reactive environment.
7. Strong visual feedback.
8. Seamless endless gameplay.

The game should have a relaxing, colorful atmosphere while becoming progressively more challenging.

12. FINAL REQUIREMENTS

Build an actual playable game, not a static visual demonstration.

Every major system must function:

- Main menu and garage.
- Both drivable vehicles.
- Vehicle switching.
- Customization.
- Touch steering.
- Traffic AI.
- Collision physics.
- Endless road generation.
- Scoring.
- Game-over and restart systems.
- Music playback and importing.
- Music-reactive scenery.
- Settings and pause menu.

Prioritize fully functioning gameplay and polished visuals.

The final result should look and feel like a professionally developed, colorful 3D mobile arcade game called ROADBOUND.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

metadata.displayText:
ROADBOUND — COMPLETE VISUAL OVERHAUL

The current version of Roadbound looks extremely unfinished. Use the attached screenshot to identify the visual problems.

Completely overhaul the game's graphics while preserving its existing functional gameplay systems, vehicle customization, radio, scoring, and controls.

This must be a substantial improvement to the actual rendered 3D gameplay, not just adjustments to colors or the interface.

1. Completely rebuild the vehicles

The current vehicles look like rectangular boxes.

Replace them with attractive, smoothly modeled, stylized low-poly vehicles.

- Create recognizable, properly proportioned cars and pickup trucks.
- Add shaped hoods, cabins, doors, bumpers, fenders, and wheel arches.
- Give vehicles actual depth and dimensional detail.
- Add realistic-looking cartoon wheels and tires.
- Use dark tinted glass with black window trim.
- Add polished chrome bumpers and reflective metallic paint.
- Ensure all body panels match in color.
- Give different traffic vehicles distinct silhouettes.
- Use smooth, visually appealing surfaces without excessive polygons.
- Make headlights and taillights properly integrated into the body.

IMPORTANT: The player vehicle must face away from the camera. The camera should show its REAR, including the tailgate and taillights, while driving forward. Fix any reversed vehicle orientations immediately.

Maintain customizable animated full-body skins. Do not add attachments or cosmetic particle effects.

2. Completely redesign the environment

The current world is far too empty, flat, and repetitive.

Build a rich, vibrant, stylized countryside with:

- Beautiful rolling hills with natural shapes.
- Dense, varied tree clusters.
- Multiple tree species with attractive rounded canopies.
- Colorful grass and vegetation.
- Flower patches and roadside bushes.
- Farmland with visible crops.
- Wooden fences and utility poles.
- Detailed cartoon barns and farmhouses.
- Rolling fields extending into distant mountains.
- Smooth terrain transitions.
- Environmental depth and atmospheric perspective.

Make the world feel handcrafted, lively, and interesting.

Avoid randomly scattering identical trees across empty flat terrain.

3. Dramatically improve lighting

Replace the washed-out pink lighting with beautiful, high-contrast golden-hour lighting.

Use:

- A large glowing orange sunset.
- Rich orange and golden sunlight.
- Purple and blue shadows.
- Warm reflections on vehicles.
- Dynamic soft shadows.
- Subtle atmospheric haze.
- Rich green vegetation.
- Deep blue-gray asphalt.
- Carefully controlled bloom.

The environment must retain its vibrant individual colors instead of everything appearing pink.

4. Completely improve the road

The current road is too straight, wide, and visually boring.

Create:

- Smooth winding highways.
- Gentle hills and elevation changes.
- Natural road curves.
- Properly proportioned traffic lanes.
- Detailed asphalt materials.
- Realistic stylized road markings.
- Road shoulders.
- Guardrails where appropriate.
- Roadside signs.
- Subtle reflections.
- More convincing road edges.

Create a convincing sense of forward movement and speed.

5. Fix the camera

Use a smooth cinematic third-person chase camera.

- Position the camera behind and above the vehicle.
- Keep the vehicle near the lower center of the screen.
- Show plenty of road ahead.
- Allow gentle camera movement during turns.
- Add subtle field-of-view changes at higher speeds.
- Keep the vehicle large enough to appreciate its design.
- Never show the front of the player vehicle during normal forward driving.

6. Redesign the interface

The current interface is oversized and distracts from the game.

- Remove the permanent giant ROADBOUND title during gameplay.
- Make the score significantly smaller.
- Use a clean, modern arcade interface.
- Keep the pause button compact.
- Make the radio interface collapsible.
- Remove unnecessary decorative text.
- Prioritize visibility of the actual driving environment.

7. Improve environmental animation

Make the world feel alive.

- Trees sway gently.
- Grass moves with the wind.
- Shadows move naturally.
- Traffic vehicles animate smoothly.
- Vehicle suspensions react to movement.
- The scenery responds to the music.
- Sunset visualizer effects pulse with the bass.

Music reactions should be clearly noticeable but tasteful.

8. Quality requirements

The final game must look like a polished, commercially released mobile arcade driving game.

Avoid:

- Primitive cube vehicles.
- Empty landscapes.
- Flat, featureless materials.
- Oversized interfaces.
- Repetitive scenery.
- Awkward camera angles.
- Washed-out lighting.
- Transparent or mismatched vehicle panels.
- Unnaturally straight roads.
- Placeholder-looking graphics.

Maintain good Android performance.

9. Implementation priorities

Make improvements in this order:

1. Fix vehicle orientation and chase camera.
2. Replace the primitive vehicle models.
3. Rebuild the terrain and roadside scenery.
4. Improve lighting, materials, and shadows.
5. Redesign the road geometry.
6. Improve the UI.
7. Refine animations and music reactions.

After completing the changes, verify the game in actual gameplay, not merely the garage or main menu.

The redesigned game should look dramatically different from the screenshot.

Do not consider this task complete if the vehicles still look like simple boxes or the environment still resembles an empty prototype.
